q1: SELECT b.name AS bar, COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker) AS num_drinker, AVG(s.price) AS avg_price, (SELECT f1.drinker FROM frequents AS f1 WHERE f1.bar = b.name ORDER BY f1.times_a_week DESC, f1.drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY num_drinker DESC, b.name ASC
q2: SELECT b.name AS bar_name, COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT f.drinker), 0) AS total_num_drinker, COALESCE(AVG(s.price), NULL) AS avg_price, (SELECT drinker FROM frequents WHERE bar = b.name GROUP BY drinker ORDER BY SUM(times_a_week) DESC, drinker ASC LIMIT 1) AS most_reg_drinker FROM bar AS b LEFT JOIN frequents AS f ON b.name = f.bar LEFT JOIN serves AS s ON b.name = s.bar GROUP BY b.name ORDER BY total_num_drinker DESC, b.name

counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('Brewery', '123 Brewery St');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent due to the handling of NULL values in the AVG() function. Q1 uses COALESCE(AVG(s.price), NULL) which results in NULL if AVG(s.price) is NULL, while Q2 uses COALESCE(AVG(s.price), 0) which results in 0 if AVG(s.price) is NULL.
counterexample_dsp: A bar that serves no beers (i.e., no entries in the Serves table) will trigger the difference.
